title: Silicon Samples Match the Answers but Not the Respondents
abstract: arXiv:2610.30900v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Silicon sampling generates survey respondents by having a large language model (LLM) answer a survey as a person with given demographic attributes, and the resulting synthetic populations are increasingly used in place of human ones. Existing evaluations focus on individual-answer accuracy, per-question answer distributions, and correlations across questions. None of these compares the respondents themselves, so a generator whose respondents have combinations of answers found in no human respondent can still score well if it reproduces every answer distribution. We propose the respondent coverage gap (RCG), which represents each respondent as a point defined by their complete answer profile and measures how far each human respondent is from the nearest generated one, relative to the distance between human samples. translated_title: 硅基样本匹配了答案，却匹配不了受访者
translated_abstract: 硅基采样通过让大语言模型（LLM）以具有特定人口统计属性的个人身份回答问卷来生成调查受访者，由此产生的合成人群正日益被用来替代真实人类人群。现有评估主要关注个体答案准确性、单个问题的答案分布以及跨问题的相关性，这些方法均无法比较受访者本身，因此即使某个生成器产生的受访者答案组合在真实人类受访者中从未出现过，只要它能复现每个问题的答案分布，仍能获得较高的评分。我们提出了“受访者覆盖差距”（respondent coverage gap, RCG），将每个受访者表示为由其完整答案组合定义的一个点，并衡量每个真实人类受访者与最近的生成样本之间的距离（相对于人类样本之间的距离）。在两项美国社会调查上，我们评估的全部六个大语言模型都未能覆盖真实人类受访者，并且在主要实验设置下，它们的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 论文提出“受访者覆盖差距”（RCG）这一新评估指标，从完整答案组合的角度衡量合成受访者与真实受访者的差异，发现六种大语言模型虽然能复现答案分布，却无法覆盖真实人类受访者的答案特征组合。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes the respondent coverage gap (RCG), a novel metric that evaluates silicon sampling by comparing complete respondent answer profiles rather than individual answers, showing that six LLMs match answer distributions but fail to cover real human respondents.
